## Investigation Report

### Verdict/Confidence/Severity/Task Type

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Verdict | CONFIRMED |
| Confidence | High |
| Severity | Medium |
| Task Type | Bug fix / regression coverage |

### What Was Claimed

Picked-up issues advance through durable phases and phase comments, but their visible `workflow:*` label remains stale. Each phase boundary should project the canonical current-state label, remove the prior workflow label, and preserve unrelated labels.

### What We Found

`GitHubIssueProjector.setWorkflowLabel` already performs a read-modify-write projection: it removes existing `workflow:*` labels, adds the requested canonical label, and retains ordinary issue labels. The parent-owned node path in `src/workflows/work-on.ts` also maps many node transitions to canonical stages.

The direct checkpoint path is incomplete. `forge_checkpoint` in `src/agents/child-runtime.ts` invokes `workflowLabelForCheckpoint` after every non-queue event, but that helper only emits labels for phase starts and investigation completion. It does not emit a canonical projection for ordinary phase completions, resolve boundaries, or the merge boundary. Consequently, a direct run can durably record a completed phase while no label reconciliation occurs at that boundary; recovery and mixed parent/child execution paths can therefore leave the previous workflow label visible.

### Root Cause

Workflow label projection is split between parent node transitions and child phase checkpoints, but the child checkpoint mapping covers only a subset of lifecycle transitions. The projection writer is capable of replacing stale workflow labels; the missing behavior is the phase-to-canonical-stage mapping and its regression coverage at every relevant boundary.

### Affected Files

| Path | Role | Finding |
|---|---|---|
| `src/agents/child-runtime.ts` | Child checkpoint side effects | `workflowLabelForCheckpoint` is the incomplete mapping used after durable phase events. |
| `src/adapters/github-projection.ts` | GitHub issue projection | Replacement semantics exist and preserve ordinary labels; no replacement redesign is required. |
| `src/workflows/work-on.ts` | Parent orchestration | Parent node mapping covers its own transitions but does not replace the child checkpoint mapping. |
| `test/adapters/github-projection.test.ts` | Projection regression tests | Verifies one investigating-to-merged replacement, but not all lifecycle transitions. |
| `test/agents/child-runtime-commit.test.ts` | Child runtime tests | Suitable location for pure checkpoint mapping coverage. |
| `test/workflows/work-on.test.ts` | Parent mapping tests | Covers partial node-stage lifecycle mapping. |

### Evidence

1. `forge_checkpoint` appends the typed event before invoking `workflowLabelForCheckpoint`; a missing mapping leaves the durable event ahead of the visible label.
2. The current helper returns `workflow:investigating` only for investigate start, `workflow:building` for selected build-phase starts, `workflow:in-review` for review start, and ready/invalid only for investigate completion.
3. `setWorkflowLabel` filters old `workflow:*` labels and writes the requested label alongside non-workflow labels, matching the replacement requirement.
4. Existing projector coverage confirms `workflow:investigating` is removed when `workflow:merged` is set and unrelated `bug`/`priority:P1` labels remain.

### History Findings

The checked-out changelog records workflow labels as an initial capability, but contains no issue-specific remediation history. The available repository guidance describes labels as human-readable projections of durable state. No related historical artifact changes the requested scope.

### Recommendation

Expand the checkpoint transition mapping to emit canonical labels for every applicable start and completion boundary: investigating, ready-to-build, building, in-review, awaiting-merge, and merged (with invalid/decomposed terminal outcomes preserved where already supported). Keep the existing read-modify-write projector semantics. Add table-driven tests covering the complete lifecycle and asserting stale workflow-label removal plus preservation of unrelated labels.

### Related Issues

None identified in the checked-out repository context.

### Decomposition Assessment

The defect is bounded to one projection mapping and its tests. No decomposition is needed; implementation can remain a single writer change within the approved worktree.

### Acceptance Spec

- [ ] Resolve/investigation boundaries project `workflow:investigating`.
- [ ] Investigation completion projects `workflow:ready-to-build` unless the typed outcome is invalid/decomposed.
- [ ] Plan, prepare-worktree, implement, and verify boundaries project `workflow:building`.
- [ ] Review boundaries project `workflow:in-review`.
- [ ] Merge start/completion project `workflow:awaiting-merge` then `workflow:merged`.
- [ ] Every transition removes prior `workflow:*` labels and preserves unrelated labels.
- [ ] Automated tests cover the lifecycle mapping and replacement behavior.

<!-- INVESTIGATION:COMPLETE -->

## Builder Contract

### Objective

Ensure every applicable direct work-on phase checkpoint projects the canonical workflow-state label at start and completion boundaries, while retaining stale-label replacement and unrelated issue-label preservation.

### Allowed Paths

- `src/agents/child-runtime.ts`
- `test/agents/child-runtime-commit.test.ts`
- `test/adapters/github-projection.test.ts`

### Forbidden Changes

- Do not change GitHub authentication, transport authority, or issue/label API endpoints.
- Do not alter durable event schemas, phase ordering, leases, review authority, merge policy, or parent-owned merge/close/cleanup behavior.
- Do not remove or rename canonical labels in `WORKFLOW_LABEL_BY_STAGE`.
- Do not remove preservation of unrelated issue labels.
- Do not add arbitrary shell commands, credentials, or side-effect capabilities to child nodes.

### Invariants

- `setWorkflowLabel` remains a read-modify-write operation that removes prior `workflow:*` labels and retains unrelated issue labels.
- A checkpoint label is projected only after its durable event is accepted.
- Investigation outcomes continue to distinguish `ready-to-build`, `invalid`, and `decomposed` routing where applicable.
- Label values remain the canonical `workflow:*` values already defined by ForgeDock.
- Repeating the same projection remains idempotent.

### Deliverables

1. A complete phase/action mapping for applicable direct checkpoints: investigating, ready-to-build, building, in-review, awaiting-merge, and merged.
2. Table-driven tests proving mapping coverage for lifecycle starts and completions, including terminal investigation outcomes.
3. Projector transition coverage proving each replacement removes stale workflow labels and preserves unrelated labels.

### Acceptance Mapping

| Check | Implementation |
|---|---|
| `label-at-phase-boundary` | Expand the child-runtime checkpoint mapping for every applicable phase start/completion. |
| `investigation-routing` | Preserve confirmed/normal ready-to-build routing and invalid/decomposed terminal routing. |
| `stale-workflow-removed` | Exercise `GitHubIssueProjector.setWorkflowLabel` across successive canonical labels. |
| `unrelated-labels-preserved` | Assert `bug`, priority, and other non-workflow labels survive every replacement. |
| `idempotent-projection` | Repeat the final lifecycle projection and assert stable labels/no duplicate workflow state. |
| `automated-coverage` | Add deterministic unit tests without network access or credentials. |

### Out of Scope

- Parent-owned node projection redesign in `src/workflows/work-on.ts`.
- New workflow states, label creation, or changes to `/forge:init`.
- Retry scheduling, GitHub concurrency locking, or projection backfills beyond the existing reconciliation path.

## Implementation Context

### Repository Guidance

The repository requires deterministic, testable workflow authority, regression tests for safety/recovery fixes, canonical ForgeDock artifacts, one writer per worktree, and fail-closed behavior. The tracked policy permits `npm run check` as the required named verification.

### Callers and Data Flow

- `forge_checkpoint` in `src/agents/child-runtime.ts` appends a typed phase event through `RunJournal`.
- For non-queue actions it projects the phase artifact/comment, derives a workflow label, and calls `GitHubIssueProjector.setWorkflowLabel`.
- `setWorkflowLabel` reads current issue labels and replaces all `workflow:*` labels through the GitHub labels endpoint while retaining ordinary labels.
- Parent node transitions in `src/workflows/work-on.ts` have a separate mapping and are intentionally outside this bounded child-checkpoint fix.

### CI Surface

- The configured required local command is `check`, which runs `npm run typecheck` and `npm test`.
- Tests use Node's test runner and in-memory GitHub transports; no network or credentials are needed.
- GitHub CI remains the parent-owned authoritative acceptance gate after PR preparation.

### Prior Findings

- Investigation confirmed that the projector already supports replacement semantics.
- The missing behavior is the incomplete `workflowLabelForCheckpoint` mapping and absent complete-lifecycle checkpoint coverage.
- No security, API-authority, or product-scope decision is required.

### Hazards

- A mapping error could leave a stale state label or misroute invalid investigations.
- A projector test transport that models only additions could fail to detect stale-label retention.
- Avoid altering `needs-human` handling or parent transition semantics because those labels and paths have separate recovery behavior.

<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT:COMPLETE -->
<!-- FORGE:ARCHITECT -->
## Architecture Plan

### Label Derivation

Keep label derivation at the existing child checkpoint boundary. Make `workflowLabelForCheckpoint` return the canonical label for both `start` and `complete` actions where the phase has a visible lifecycle state:

| Phase boundary | Canonical label |
|---|---|
| `resolve` start/complete | `workflow:investigating` |
| `investigate` start | `workflow:investigating` |
| `investigate` complete (normal) | `workflow:ready-to-build` |
| `investigate` complete (invalid) | `workflow:invalid` |
| `investigate` complete (decomposed) | `workflow:decomposed` |
| `plan`, `prepare-worktree`, `implement`, `verify` start/complete | `workflow:building` |
| `review` start/complete | `workflow:in-review` |
| `merge` start | `workflow:awaiting-merge` |
| `merge` complete | `workflow:merged` |

The current direct work-on contract keeps merge, close, and cleanup parent-owned; merge mappings are defensive and do not grant child merge authority.

### Test Strategy

1. Export the pure checkpoint label helper (or an equivalent testable pure mapping) without exposing GitHub side effects.
2. Add table-driven assertions for every listed phase/action and investigation outcome.
3. Extend the in-memory projector lifecycle test through investigating → ready-to-build → building → in-review → awaiting-merge → merged, asserting exactly one workflow label and preservation of unrelated labels after every step.
4. Keep the existing idempotency/read-back tests unchanged except where shared assertions are reused.

### Implementation Sequence

1. Update the child-runtime mapping with explicit phase/action cases and case-insensitive terminal-outcome handling consistent with canonical reports.
2. Add pure mapping coverage for normal and terminal outcomes.
3. Add full projector transition coverage with stale workflow labels and unrelated labels.
4. Run the named `check` verification, inspect the resulting diff, and commit only the allowed files.

### Review Risks

Correctness review should verify that every direct checkpoint boundary has exactly one canonical mapping and that invalid/decomposed outcomes cannot regress to ready-to-build. Security review should verify the change is pure label selection and does not expand child-side GitHub capability or alter label preservation beyond the accepted contract.

<!-- FORGE:ARCHITECT:COMPLETE -->
